revision_notes: The single cited source (a PATNUC promotional post on agricultural digitisation) was fetched and confirms no AI/data-exchange content, so it does not itself support any score above Unknown. A fresh search found Cameroon's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (SNIA), unveiled by MINPOSTEL in July 2025 and tracked by OECD.AI, whose 'data infrastructure' pillar explicitly calls for a government Data Lake, mass digitisation of public services and national interoperability standards — i.e. a concrete plan to bring AI/analytics to cross-government data exchange. revised_comments: Cameroon's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (SNIA), unveiled by the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications in July 2025, includes a dedicated data and digital infrastructure pillar calling for a government Data Lake, mass digitisation of public services and national interoperability standards, indicating that AI-enabled analytics for cross-government data exchange are at the planning stage. No operational data exchange platform currently incorporates AI for data quality assurance, fraud detection or predictive analytics.

Comments: PATNuC project has a public website (patnuc.cm) and MINPOSTEL publishes some information. No public dashboard on data exchange operations found. Limited disclosure on interconnected systems.
redteam_note: Value Name differs from the scale label — usually cosmetic.
revision_notes: Both original sources were fetched: the PATNUC post is a general programme overview with no transparency-specific content, and the cited MINPOSTEL page is a general digital-economy news feed rather than reporting on data-exchange operations specifically, so they only weakly support the score. A fresh search found a November 2025 PATNUC account of a draft e-Gov law (examined at a workshop in Ebolowa) that would create a general right of access to public information and place interoperability governance under a newly announced body, GovTech Cameroun; a December 2025 Digital Business Africa report confirms the wider e-Gov project is still not implemented. No public dashboard or annual report on data exchange operations, governance or data-sharing agreements was found to exist yet, so the score of 2 (Low - Limited Disclosure) is confirmed, with the evidence base updated to 2025.
revised_comments: Public transparency regarding Cameroon's government data exchange remains limited. The World Bank-funded PATNUC programme, under the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications, maintains a public website with project updates, and the ministry periodically publishes general digital-economy news, but no public dashboard or annual report specifically covering data exchange or interoperability operations, governance, or data-sharing agreements is available. A draft e-Gov law, discussed at a PATNUC workshop in Ebolowa in November 2025, proposes a general right of access to public information and would place interoperability governance under a newly established body, GovTech Cameroun, but as of late 2025 this reform had not yet been enacted or implemented.
